l1.title: One, two, three
l1.hook: I'm drawing the valley. Look, leaves!
l1.atlas: The valley is on the map! One, two, three: you can see them right away.

model.s1: I look at all the leaves at once: three.
model.s2: I look for three dots. There they are!

t1.hint: Show the same number on your fingers.
t1.explain: Two stones. You can tell right away. Two!

t2.prompt: Match each pile to its dots.
t2.hint: See how many, then find that many dots.
t2.explain: One stone, two berries, three leaves.

t3.hint: Look at all the berries at once.
t3.explain: The berries are spread out, but there are still three.

t4.prompt: Match the piles with the same number.
t4.hint: Stones or berries? Just count how many.
t4.explain: One and one, two and two, three and three.

l2.title: Counting to five
l2.hook: I'm counting everything for the map. Will you help?
l2.atlas: The map is bigger now: we counted up to five!

model.s1: I count: one, two, three, four.
model.s2: The last number is four. So there are four!

t1.prompt: Count the stones. How many are there?
t1.explain: One, two, three, four, five. Five!

t2.prompt: Put the piles in order: three, four, five.
t2.hint: Pick a pile, count it, then place it.

t3.hint: Look at all the berries at once.
t3.explain: Two berries. You can tell right away. Two!

t4.prompt: Match each pile to its number.
t4.hint: Count a pile. Which number is it?
t4.explain: Five berries, three stones, four leaves.

l3.title: Counting to ten
l3.hook: I lost count! Shall we count the leaves one by one?
l3.atlas: Together we counted all the way to ten!

model.s1: One, two, three, four, five, six!
model.s2: The last number is six. So there are six!

t1.prompt: How many stones? Count them one by one.
t1.hint: Touch each stone once as you count.
t1.explain: The last number is seven. There are seven!

t2.prompt: Put the piles in order: one, three, five.
t2.hint: Count: which pile has three, and which has five?

t3.prompt: How many leaves? Count them all.
t3.hint: Count the top row first, then the bottom row.
t3.explain: The last number is ten. There are ten!

t4.hint: How many in the pile? Find that number.
t4.explain: Five here, two here, and four here!

num-l1.title: Numerals up to five
num-l1.hook: I label the piles with numerals. Look!
num-l1.atlas: Every pile up to five has its own numeral.

model.s2: Three leaves, and this is numeral three.

t1.hint: Count the pile, then find that numeral.
t1.explain: Four stones. This is numeral four!

t2.prompt: Match each pile to its numeral.
t2.hint: Count the pile, then look for the numeral.
t2.explain: One stone, five berries, three leaves.

t3.prompt: How many berries? Pick the numeral.
t3.hint: Look at the berries all at once.
t3.explain: Two berries. This is numeral two!

t4.hint: Count on from two. Which comes first?

num-l2.title: Zero
num-l2.hook: Help me: which basket is empty?

model.prompt: How many are in the basket?
model.s1: The basket is empty. Nothing inside.
model.s2: Empty means zero. Here is zero!

t1.explain: Here it is: nothing inside. That is zero!

t2.prompt: Match each basket to its numeral.
t2.hint: How many are in the basket? Find that number.
t2.explain: Empty is zero, one berry, two leaves.

t3.prompt: How many leaves? Pick the numeral.
t3.hint: Touch each leaf as you count.
t3.explain: Five leaves. This is numeral five!

t4.prompt: Put the baskets in order: zero, one, two.
t4.hint: Count what is in the basket, then place it.

num-l3.title: Numerals up to ten
num-l3.hook: I mixed up two numerals that look alike!
num-l3.atlas: All the numerals up to ten are in place.

model.s1: Counting one by one: seven stones.

t1.hint: Count one by one to the end.
t1.explain: Nine: a circle on top, a tail going down.

t2.hint: Count on from five. Which comes first?

t3.hint: Count what is in the basket. Where is that number?
t3.explain: Empty is zero, two berries, three stones.

t4.hint: Touch each stone once, to the end.
t4.explain: Ten is a one and a zero side by side!

consent.title: Everything stays on this device
consent.body: Nothing goes online until you turn it on. Lessons played, skills and the in-game name live here. To pick the next lessons and show you what is working, the app remembers which lessons were played, when and how long they took. Lesson records are kept for 12 months. You can delete everything in Data. To refuse, close the setup: nothing will remain on the device.

policy.title: Privacy policy
policy.body: Draft. The app keeps the child's data only on this device: lessons played, skills, in-game name, settings and the consent log. Nothing is sent online. Lesson records are deleted after 12 months. A parent can delete data in Data; export arrives with the cloud copy. Final text follows legal review.
